# Children survive deletion of their parent work item and become unreachable orphans

> **Migrated** from the SorraAgents worklog item **SA-0MW7Z1PR20094WIS** (2026-11-13) after the producer approved migrating it here, accepting the re-scope and deleting the SorraAgents original. Provenance for the orphan census below is the SorraAgents worklog; the engineering scope is entirely in this repository.

## Summary

Deleting a parent work item does not dispose of its open children. They survive as **orphans**: their `parentId` points at an id that no longer resolves (or resolves only to a soft-deleted item), so they appear in no rollup, are never closed by the parent's closure path, and are invisible to every parent-level report.

## Evidence (2026-11-08 SorraAgents backlog review)

55 of 444 open-scope items had an unresolvable parent:

| Lost parent | Resolution | Open children |
|---|---|---|
| `SA-0MSC7QZQL006Q747` | hard-deleted (id not found at all) | 46 |
| `SA-0MLDAXNBQ17OA9PT` "Scheduler Configuration & Scoping" | soft-deleted | 5 |
| `SA-0MLPU8H3B1LWK3B3` "Add closing of work item to cleanup skill" | soft-deleted | 3 |
| `SA-0ML7NOSHP0MJC6HS` "AMPA Daemon: Discord heartbeat & notifier" | soft-deleted | 1 |

The 46 hard-deleted orphans were all refactor findings from 2026-08-02, filed under a scan-batch parent that was removed while its children stayed behind; the oldest were 258 days old. None surfaced in any progress view, and none could be closed by the normal "parent closes when all children close" path — the parent was already gone.

`wl delete` is recursive by default (documented), and `--no-recursive` is the documented "leaving children orphaned" opt-out, but a hard delete evidently bypassed the children; the exact route that produced the 46-item batch is confirmed below as `wl doctor prune` / `foreign-items --apply` (see R1).

## Re-scope (producer-approved 2026-11-13)

Investigation of this repo (main @ `77264ee6a`) shows the original acceptance criteria are **substantially shipped**, which narrows the work:

- **Recursive delete ships.** `wl delete` is recursive by default, has an explicit `--no-recursive` opt-out, records `--reason`, and reports the deleted descendants — `src/commands/delete.ts` (WL-0MQFZ81MO000QSRL).
- **Doctor already flags orphans.** Root `wl doctor` (`validate`) emits a distinct per-item finding via `validateParentReferences()`: code `parent.missing-endpoint`, type `missing-parent`, carrying the lost parent id in `context.parentId` and a safe `parentId: null` proposed fix — `src/doctor/parent-check.ts`, `src/commands/doctor/validate.ts`.
- **Promotion path exists.** `wl doctor dangling-parents [--apply]` detects dangling parents and detaches them (`parentId -> null`) — `src/commands/doctor/dangling-parents.ts` (WL-0MUJM2LV1000IHKR), and `wl update <id> --parent null` detaches instead of writing `WL-NULL`.

The remaining defects are therefore narrower than the originally filed five ACs:

- **R1 — hard-delete admin paths still orphan children silently.** `wl doctor prune` hard-deletes each candidate via `store.deleteWorkItem(id)` with no descendant handling (`src/commands/doctor/prune.ts`); `wl doctor foreign-items --apply` (`applyForeignItemCleanup`, `src/doctor/foreign-items-check.ts`) likewise deletes each id individually and, although it cascades audit results and FTS entries, it neither cascades to nor refuses when an own-prefix child points at the deleted id.
- **R2 — promotion/detach loses the history.** `wl doctor dangling-parents --apply` contains no comment/attribution call, and neither `wl doctor --fix` nor `wl update <id> --parent null` records the previous parent or the rationale.
- **R3 — orphan reporting is not grouped.** Findings are emitted per child; there is no grouped summary keyed by lost-parent id carrying the count and child ids.
- **R3b — children of a *soft-deleted* parent are not reported at all.** `validateParentReferences` resolves `parentId` against `db.getAll()`, which includes soft-deleted rows (proved by `prune` filtering `status === 'deleted'` out of the same collection), so a soft-deleted parent looks resolvable. 9 of the 55 evidence orphans fell in this class.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every hard-delete admin path that can leave children without a resolvable parent (notably `wl doctor prune`; audit `wl doctor foreign-items --apply` and any other store-level `deleteWorkItem` caller) either cascades to descendants or refuses without an explicit opt-in, so no silent orphaning remains.
2. Any explicit orphaning opt-in (`wl delete --no-recursive`) records a comment on each orphaned child naming the previous parent and the explicit decision.
3. `wl doctor` reports orphans as a distinct finding that includes the lost-parent id and the child id — including children whose parent is soft-deleted (R3b); `wl doctor dangling-parents --dry-run` summarises the grouped count of children per lost-parent id.
4. Promotion (`parentId -> null`, via `wl doctor --fix`, `wl doctor dangling-parents --apply`, or `wl update --parent null`) records a comment naming the previous parent and the rationale (promote-because-live vs retire-because-stale), so the history is not lost.
5. The retention rule — promote when the child's subject is still live; retire when it is superseded, its target is gone, or the abandoned parent's feature was never delivered — is documented alongside the remediation path.
6. Automated tests cover: pruning a parent with children does not orphan them; explicit orphaning records the previous parent; doctor output names the lost parent and the children (including the soft-deleted-parent case); promotion clears `parentId`, keeps the children reachable, and records the comment.
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes (CLI/doctor docs and the remediation/retention guidance).
8. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Work can no longer disappear from every view because its parent was removed, so nothing sits in the queue invisible and unclosable.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (now evidenced):** the 46-item hard-deleted batch came from a single-id hard-delete admin path — `wl doctor prune` is the leading candidate; `foreign-items --apply` can produce the same shape for own-prefix children.
- **Risk:** changing prune/foreign-items cascade behaviour could delete more than intended — mitigate with a dry-run-first default and an explicit opt-in for destructive cascades.
- **Risk (scope creep):** incidental doctor/delete cleanups discovered during the fix should be filed as separate items, not folded in.
- The delete-reason attribution defect is already fixed by **WL-0MW8078CA006Q2P7** (completed) and is out of scope here; do not re-open or re-implement it.

## Constraints

- Do **not** re-implement already-shipped behaviour (recursive `wl delete`, the `parent.missing-endpoint` doctor finding, `--parent null` detach); build only the residual gaps R1–R3b.
- CHANGELOG is managed by the ship release pipeline, not this item.

## Existing state

- `wl delete` recursive-by-default with `--no-recursive` and `--reason` (`src/commands/delete.ts`; WL-0MQFZ81MO000QSRL).
- `wl doctor` root `validate` includes `validateParentReferences()` → `parent.missing-endpoint` / `missing-parent` findings with a safe `parentId: null` fix (`src/doctor/parent-check.ts`, `src/commands/doctor/validate.ts`).
- `wl doctor dangling-parents [--dry-run|--apply]` detaches dangling parents (`src/commands/doctor/dangling-parents.ts`, WL-0MUJM2LV1000IHKR).
- `wl doctor prune` hard-deletes a single id via `store.deleteWorkItem(id)` with no descendant handling (`src/commands/doctor/prune.ts`) — the residual orphaning route.
- `wl doctor foreign-items --apply` hard-deletes with a "full cascade" limited to audit results + FTS entries (`src/doctor/foreign-items-check.ts`).

## Desired change

Close the residual gaps: make hard-delete admin paths cascade-or-refuse (R1), record the previous parent + decision whenever a child is orphaned or promoted (R2), and report orphans grouped by lost-parent id — including soft-deleted parents — in `wl doctor` output (R3/R3b), with a documented retention/remediation rule and tests.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/commands/doctor/prune.ts` — cascade to descendants or refuse when pruning a parent that still has children.
- `src/doctor/foreign-items-check.ts` — same guard for `foreign-items --apply` when an own-prefix child points at a foreign id.
- `src/doctor/parent-check.ts` — treat soft-deleted parents as unresolvable; emit the grouped orphan finding (lost-parent id, count, child ids).
- `src/commands/doctor/validate.ts` — grouped orphan summary and comment-on-detach for `--fix`.
- `src/commands/doctor/dangling-parents.ts` — grouped count per lost parent in `--dry-run` and comment on detach in `--apply`.
- `src/commands/delete.ts` — comment on each child when `--no-recursive` orphaning is applied.
- `src/commands/update.ts` — comment on `--parent null` detach naming the previous parent.
- `CLI.md`, `DOCTOR_AND_MIGRATIONS.md` — retention rule and remediation path.

## Proposed decomposition (plan input — not yet created)

Test-first ordering; each is a vertical slice (code + tests + docs):

1. **Orphan-guard failing test fixtures** (task, test-first) — shared fixtures for a hard-deleted parent, a soft-deleted parent, a foreign-prefix parent with an own child, and a promotion; tests assert the target behaviours and fail on current main.
2. **Hard-delete paths cascade-or-refuse** (R1, AC1) — `wl doctor prune` refuses (or requires an explicit `--cascade-children` opt-in) when a candidate still has live children; same audit for `foreign-items --apply`; regression tests + `DOCTOR_AND_MIGRATIONS.md`.
3. **Grouped orphan reporting** (R3/R3b, AC3) — treat soft-deleted parents as unresolvable, add a grouped finding carrying lost-parent id, child count and child ids, and a grouped summary in `dangling-parents --dry-run`; tests.
4. **Attribution comments on orphan/promote** (R2, AC2/AC4) — `wl delete --no-recursive` comments each orphaned child; `wl update --parent null`, `dangling-parents --apply` and `doctor --fix` comment naming the previous parent plus the promote-vs-retire rationale; tests.
5. **Retention & remediation docs** (AC5/AC7) — document the promote-when-live / retire-when-superseded rule alongside the remediation path in `CLI.md` and `DOCTOR_AND_MIGRATIONS.md`; AC8 is verified at the dev-push gate.

## Related work

- **WL-0MQFZ81MO000QSRL** (completed) — recursive deletion of work items with children.
- **WL-0MUJM2LV1000IHKR** (completed) — treat `--parent null` as detach instead of a bogus `WL-NULL` parent.
- **WL-0MW8078CA006Q2P7** (completed) — `wl delete` delete-reason attribution (out of scope).
- **SA-0MQFXG76T000A3LR**, **SA-0MW7Z1YE9004P41D** (SorraAgents, completed) — the follow-up and the 2026-11-08 backlog triage that retired the 55 orphans found in the evidence.

## Open questions

None — the migration, the re-scope and the disposition of the SorraAgents original were all answered by the producer (see Appendix).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (migration):** "Should this item migrate to the Worklog CLI project (`ContextHub`), where all target files live, or remain in SorraAgents as a cross-project tracking item?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-11-13): migrate.** Delete the SorraAgents item once migrated. This item is the migrated copy.
- **Q2 (re-scope):** "Confirm the narrowed ACs (residual gaps R1–R3) rather than the original five?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-11-13): accept.** ACs above are the accepted re-scope, with R3b folded into AC3. Research: recursive delete (WL-0MQFZ81MO000QSRL), `--parent null` detach (WL-0MUJM2LV1000IHKR) and the `parent.missing-endpoint` finding all ship.
- **Q3 (disposition):** "If Q1 approves migration, should this SorraAgents item be closed as 'moved' with a link to the new WL item, or kept open?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-11-13): delete it** (not kept as a tracking record). Done: SA-0MW7Z1PR20094WIS was deleted with a reason naming this item.

## Impact (provenance)

Migrated item — original SorraAgents item SA-0MW7Z1PR20094WIS, tags `worklog`, `backlog-hygiene`, `discovered-from`; priority high; effort Medium / risk Medium (estimate carried over).

# Orphan-guard failing test fixtures

Test-first task: shared fixtures and failing tests for the orphan-guard behaviours targeted by WL-0MWFMKWZA005ZT4T.

## Goal

Establish the test harness that asserts the target behaviours and fails on current main, proving each residual gap (R1, R2, R3, R3b) before implementation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Fixtures cover: a hard-deleted parent with live children; a soft-deleted parent with live children; a foreign-prefix parent with an own-prefix child; and a promotion (`parentId -> null`).
- Tests assert that `wl doctor prune` on a parent with live children does NOT orphan them (either cascades or refuses) — fails on current main.
- Tests assert explicit orphaning (`wl delete --no-recursive`) records a comment naming the previous parent — fails on current main.
- Tests assert `wl doctor` output names the lost parent id and child ids, including the soft-deleted-parent case (R3b) — fails on current main.
- Tests assert promotion clears `parentId`, keeps children reachable, and records a comment naming the previous parent and rationale — fails on current main.
- Tests run green after the subsequent implementation features land.

## Key Files

- `src/commands/doctor/prune.ts`
- `src/doctor/parent-check.ts`
- `src/commands/delete.ts`

## Notes

Parent: WL-0MWFMKWZA005ZT4T (work stream: children surviving parent deletion). Test-first ordering is mandated by the parent plan.

impl child of WL-0MWH56SWX004HSKQ (blocked-by the AC1/AC3/AC4 test child).

## Goal

As an operator relying on the downtime dispatcher, I want the hydrator's
"is this item being worked on?" evidence to be workspace-agnostic, so a pane in
the Dispatcher workspace keeps the claim it proves.

## Scope (parent fix A + B + D)

- **Wider read.** Add a workspace-agnostic pane seam to `HydratorDeps`
  (`listAllActivePanes(): Promise<HydratorPane[] | null>`, optional so existing
  test fakes keep compiling byte-for-byte — mirroring the `hasLiveClaimHolder`
  optional-seam pattern). Production wiring: one machine-wide `herdr pane list`
  per tick, reusing the existing machine parser
  (`parseMachinePaneListOutput` from `dispatcher-anchor.cli-parsers.ts` /
  `listMachinePanes` from `dispatcher-anchor.herdr-cli.ts`) — no new parser, no
  per-item spawn.
- **One filter per question.** The demotion pane set becomes
  `collectPaneWorkItemIds(allPanes)` (no workspace argument). The display path
  (`applyActivePaneMarkers` / `markItemsActiveByPane`) keeps
  `collectPaneWorkItemIds(panes, workspaceId)` untouched.
- **Fail-open when the wider read is unavailable (parent fix B).** A `null`/
  throwing/timed-out wider read aborts the cycle with
  `reason: 'pane list unavailable (no demotion on ambiguous evidence)'` — the
  claim is kept, no release comment is written. When the seam is absent
  (legacy fakes), behaviour is exactly today's.
- **Prep-tier contract recorded (parent fix D / AC7).** Header comment states:
  `/skill:intake`, `/skill:plan` and audit runs hold **no** per-child claim lock,
  so for those tiers pane evidence is the only busy signal; the claim-holder
  probe remains the second signal only where a lock exists; ambiguity keeps the
  claim.
- Keep the step label coverage and `HYDRATOR_STEP_TIMEOUT_MS` budget unchanged;
  the wider read replaces the scoped read for demotion (still exactly ONE pane
  spawn per tick).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Parent AC1** — **Cross-workspace pane prevents release.** With a pane titled `Downtime triggered plan … - WL-XXXX` alive in the **Dispatcher** workspace and the item `in-progress` with `assignee: dispatcher`, `runHydrationOnce` makes **no** release and writes no `released because no matching pane` comment. Regression test reproduces today's exact state (plugin workspace `w5M`, pane in `w6B`). — Delivered here as the red regression test in `hydrator.test.ts` asserting `demoted === 0` and zero `applyDemotion` calls.
- **Parent AC4** — **Fail-open on an unreadable wider read.** When the cross-workspace pane read fails/returns null, the hydrator does not release (keeps the claim) and does not spam release comments. Pinned by a test. — Delivered here as the injected-clock test that withholds the release while the wider pane read returns null or throws.
- **Parent AC7** — **Prep-tier signal contract recorded.** The chosen contract for prep/audit tiers (Root cause 2: pane evidence only, or a recorded claim holder) is documented in the hydrator header comment and covered by a test for whichever option is chosen. — Delivered here as the prep-tier pane-only contract test and the `hydrator.ts` header contract text.
- **Parent AC10** — **No latency regression.** The wider pane read reuses the existing pane-list call where possible (no new per-item spawn); hydrator step budgets (`HYDRATOR_STEP_TIMEOUT_MS`) and the responsiveness suite stay green. — Delivered here as the single-pane-spawn assertion and the responsiveness suite staying green.

- `runHydrationOnce` makes no release for an item whose only pane is in another workspace (the AC1 test child goes green).
- The display marker path still ignores out-of-workspace panes (AC2 test child stays green).
- A genuinely pane-less item is still released to `open`/`intake_complete` with today's comment text (AC3 test child stays green).
- An unavailable/`null`/timed-out wider read keeps the claim, writes no release comment, and returns `ok: false` with a named reason (AC4 test child goes green).
- Exactly one pane-list spawn per hydrate tick (asserted via the recording exec harness in `hydrator.fixtures.ts`), and no `--workspace` filter is passed on the demotion read.
- The `hydrator.ts` header comment records the prep-tier pane-only contract and the fail-open rule.

## Minimal Implementation

- `hydrator.ts`: extend `HydratorDeps`, `createProductionHydratorDeps`, `runHydrationOnce`; update the header comment block.
- Production parser reuse from `dispatcher-anchor.cli-parsers.ts` / `dispatcher-anchor.herdr-cli.ts`.
- No change to `worklist.ts` / `index.ts` wiring — the demotion read is internal to the hydrator deps.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.cli-parsers.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.herdr-cli.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.fixtures.ts`

## Non-goals

- Changing placement precedence, `pane-title.ts`, or making display markers cross-workspace.
- Adding a second pane spawn per tick.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the AC1/AC3/AC4 test child (test-first).

## Impact

An operator no longer sees a dispatched prep (intake/plan) item bounce back into the dispatch pool seconds after its pane spawns in the Dispatcher workspace, because the hydrator now treats a live pane anywhere on the host as proof the item is being worked.

## Implementation notes

- Added the optional `listAllActivePanes()` seam to `HydratorDeps` (workspace-agnostic `herdr pane list`, no `--workspace`) reusing `parseMachinePaneListOutput`; production wires exactly one machine-wide pane read per tick.
- `runHydrationOnce` uses the wider seam for demotion and asks `collectPaneWorkItemIds(panes)` with no workspace filter; the display path keeps `collectPaneWorkItemIds(panes, workspaceId)` untouched. Absent seam falls back to the legacy scoped read/filter byte-for-byte.
- Fail-open: null/throwing/timed-out wider read aborts the cycle with no demotion (claim kept, no release comment).
- Header comment records the prep-tier pane-only contract (no per-child lock for intake/plan/audit; pane evidence is the only signal) and the fail-open rule.
- Flipped the five cross-workspace `it.fails` red witnesses to plain `it`; added prep-tier pane-only contract tests and a single-pane-spawn/no-`--workspace` assertion.

## Goal

Land the **test-only safety net** for the anchor self-healing work before any
production file changes, so the behaviour we must *not* regress (dead pane with
a live workspace re-resolves; an unreadable herdr fails closed and provisions
nothing; two racing callers create exactly one workspace) is pinned by tests
that are green against today's tree.

Parent: WL-0MWH50EN4007C6YH (parent AC2 and the duplicate-workspace half of
parent AC3).

## Context

The parent's regression risk is asymmetric: the fix touches the shared
provisioning path (`getDispatcherAnchor`) and adds a recovery branch to
`getDispatcherTabAnchor`, both of which already carry carefully-tuned
fail-closed semantics. The recorded pre-fix state (workspace `w6A` gone, anchor
files pointing at it) must be reusable verbatim by the sibling item that
implements the fix, so it is committed here as a shared fixture.

Evidence for the fixture shape (from the parent item, 2026-11-15):

```json
// downtime-dispatch-anchor.json
{"paneId":"w6A:p1","workspaceId":"w6A"}
// downtime-dispatch-tab-anchors.json
{"workspaceId":"w6A","byPrefix":{"WL":{"tabId":"w6A:t2","paneId":"w6A:p5"}}}
```

A pre-fix backup also exists on the live machine at
`~/.herdr/downtime/backup-anchors-20261115T011052Z/` — do not depend on that
path from a test; commit the contents as literals.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A committed fixture reproduces the recorded pre-fix anchor state exactly
   (both files, both ids `w6A`), exposed for reuse by the sibling fix item — no
   test reads `~/.herdr`.
2. **Dead pane still heals (parent AC2).** The existing behaviour is preserved:
   a persisted prefix entry whose pane is dead (workspace alive) still
   re-resolves/re-creates the tab and persists the new mapping. Pinned as a
   passing test against today's tree so the fast path cannot regress.
3. **No duplicate workspaces — a transient/unreadable herdr still fails closed**
   (parent AC3, first half). When `tab list`/`pane list` is unreadable (CLI error
   or unparseable output), `getDispatcherTabAnchor` returns `null` with
   `anchor-unavailable` and provisions nothing: `createWorkspace` is **never**
   called. Pinned as a passing test against today's tree.
4. **No duplicate workspaces — concurrent first-dispatchers create at most one**
   (parent AC3, second half). Two concurrent `getDispatcherAnchor` callers with a
   stale anchor produce exactly one `createWorkspace` call (coordination lock plus
   double-check) and both receive the same anchor; pinned as a passing test
   against today's tree, because the fix must reuse this mechanism, not replace
   it.
5. No production file is modified by this item; the full existing suite stays
   green.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add a `describe('regression fixtures: stale anchors (WL-0MWH50EN4007C6YH)')`
  block to `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.test.ts` with a shared
  `seedStaleAnchorState(tmpDir)` helper writing the two recorded files.
- Pin AC2/AC3 above with injected deps only (`vi.fn()`), following the existing
  stale-pane cases in that file.
- For AC4, drive two concurrent `getDispatcherAnchor` calls against a stale
  persisted anchor and assert `createWorkspace` was called once (the
  coordination lock is already exercised through `HERDR_COORDINATION_DIR`).
- Extend `tests/herdr/dispatcher-anchor.integration.test.ts` only if the
  end-to-end fixture is not already reachable there; otherwise leave it alone.

**Key Files:**
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.test.ts` — new fixture + three guard tests.
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.contract.ts` — read-only (fixture shapes).
- `tests/herdr/dispatcher-anchor.integration.test.ts` — only if an integration
  seam is needed.

## Dependencies

None. Must land **before** the fix items (test-first ordering).

## Out of scope

- Any production code change (including the workspace probe).
- The AC1 stale-**workspace** regression (it is red today by definition and
  lands with the fix).
## Impact

Dispatchers now get a committed regression fixture and green guard tests pinning the three behaviours the self-healing fix must not break: a dead pane in a live workspace still re-provisions its tab, an unreadable herdr still fails closed without provisioning anything, and two racing first-dispatchers still create exactly one workspace.
